headlines.title: Google's AI is winning. Search is paying for it.
headlines.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon now tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and Google Cloud revenue more than doubled, yet Alphabet stock opened down nearly 12% as search fell below half of revenue. Host Ejaaz Ahamadeen breaks down why AI is eating search, Google's ad auction change, its TPU customers and why the market may be wrong.

headlines.title: QUALCOMM (QCOM) Offers AI, Automotive, and Edge-Computing Growth Potential, Ariel Global Fund Says
headlines.summary: Ariel Investments, an investment management company, released its “Ariel Global Fund” Q3 2026 investor letter. The Fund declined in the third quarter of 2026 as renewed geopolitical tensions, higher oil prices, and elevated interest rates contributed to uneven performance across global markets. The Fund’s Investor Class returned -1.

headlines.title: QCOM Stock Earnings Preview: What to Expect From Qualcomm’s Q4 Report
headlines.summary: Qualcomm’s near-term growth outlook remains challenged by persistent weakness in the Android smartphone market and a lower revenue contribution from Apple.

headlines.title: Anthropic got hacked again, and this time we know who did it
headlines.summary: A months-old start-up founded by former DOGE staffers used AI agents to get inside Anthropic through third-party business software, reaching meeting transcripts, salaries and Slack messages. Host Ejaaz Ahamadeen breaks down who Cathedral is, how the back door worked, why Anthropic is pushing back and why every company should worry.

headlines.title: ON Semiconductor Falls 5%, NXP Semiconductors Drops 4% as Soft Guidance Revives Auto Chip Worries; Skyworks Ticks Up, Qualcomm and Texas Instruments Dip
headlines.summary: NXP Semiconductors beat earnings estimates but its cautious outlook sent auto-exposed chipmakers sliding, and the ripple effect is hitting ON Semiconductor harder than NXP itself. Whether that selloff signals a broader auto chip downturn or a buying opportunity depends on what ON Semiconductor's next report reveals.

description: QUALCOMM Incorporated engages in the development and commercialization of foundational technologies for the wireless industry worldwide. It operates through three segments: Qualcomm CDMA Technologies (QCT); Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL); and Qualcomm Strategic Initiatives (QSI). The QCT segment develops and supplies integrated circuits and system software with connectivity and computing technologies for use in mobile devices; automotive systems for connectivity, digital cockpit, and ADAS/AD; and IoT, including consumer electronic devices, industrial devices, and edge networking products. The QTL segment grants licenses or provides rights to use portions of its intellectual property portfolio, which include various patent rights useful in the manufacture and sale of wireless products comprising products implementing LTE, and/or OFDMA-based 5G products and derivatives; to use cellular standard-essential patents, including 3G, 4G and 5G for cellular devices. The QSI segment invests in early-stage companies in various industries, including 5G, artificial intelligence, automotive, consumer, enterprise, cloud, IoT, and extended reality, and investments, including non-marketable equity securities and, to a lesser extent, marketable equity securities, and convertible debt instruments. It also provides development, and other services and sells related products to the United States government agencies and their contractors. In addition, the company is also involved in Qualcomm government technologies and data center businesses. Further, it provides security and intelligence services for unmanaged networks through software-based network security solutions. The company is in collaboration with Amazon to enable customized silicon at scale for large-scale AI data centers. QUALCOMM Incorporated was incorporated in 1985 and is headquartered in San Diego, California.
